subject: biology
title: Ecology Adventure 1: Energy flow and food webs
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace energy through ecosystems — and lose 90% at each step.
meta_desc: IBDP Biology Ecology — producers, consumers, decomposers, food webs, 10% energy transfer.
final_note: You learned producers fix solar energy, ~10% transfers between trophic levels, and pyramids show energy loss as heat.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Energy flows one way:

Sun → producers (plants, algae, cyanobacteria) → primary consumers (herbivores) → secondary → tertiary.

Decomposers (fungi, bacteria) recycle nutrients from dead matter back to producers.

Only ~10% of energy passes between trophic levels. The rest is lost as:
- Heat (respiration)
- Undigested matter (egestion)
- Movement

This caps food chains at 4-5 levels. NPP = GPP − respiration. Tropical rainforests have highest NPP (~2200 g m⁻² yr⁻¹).

Pyramid of energy (units: kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹) always shrinks upward — second law of thermodynamics.

Pyramid of biomass usually shrinks but can invert (e.g. ocean plankton — small but rapid turnover).

Pyramid of numbers can be inverted (one tree → many insects).

mcqs.q: Approximately what fraction of energy passes between trophic levels?
Which group recycles nutrients from dead matter?

numericals.q: Producers fix 50,000 kJ m⁻². If 10% transfers each level, how much energy reaches the tertiary consumers (3rd consumer level)?
